newsitem.title: TURKEY: Withholding tax to raise t-bill yields -Turk banks.
newsitem.headline: Withholding tax to raise t-bill yields -Turk banks.

text.p: Turkish bankers said a 10-percent withholding tax to be imposed on Treasury bill and bonds with a 1997 maturity as part of the government's second resource package would create upward pressure on t-bill yields.
"T-bills to be auctioned with 1997 maturity will be subject to the 10-percent tax and thus, this 10-percent margin will be added onto their yields," said a private banker, who declined to be named.
"The Treasury may have difficulty in selling these new issues, so their yields may go up more than 10 percent due to weak demand," he added.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan presented on Thursday the government's second revenue-raising package aiming to earn another $10 billion in three years. The first package was disclosed on July 31.
The package, aiming to mobilise 11 categories of resources, included the withholding tax on interest income from Treasury bills and bonds to be issued with a 1997 maturity.
The tax will go into effect after a related government decree is published in the Official Gazette and will not be retroactive.
Bankers said t-bill yields fell a few points across the board on Thursday afternoon on buying in outstanding papers because they will be exempt from the new tax.
"Yields continued to ease today amid activity in existing papers," said one banker.
Other markets were unmoved by the package as markets awaited its implementation since the first package failed to raise optimism.
